articles.title: Amazon’s Bhavana Chandrashekhar to speak at RoboBusiness’ Women in Robotics Lunch
articles.summary: Amazon Robotics senior manager Bhavana Chandrashekhar will speak at RoboBusiness 2026’s Women in Robotics Lunch and participate in a keynote on AI in production robotics. The article highlights Amazon’s work on autonomous manipulation robots for warehouses, including Robin, which has picked several billion packages, and Vulcan Stow, which has stowed over a million items.
articles.advisor_relevance: The article is primarily an event announcement, but it includes useful real-world adoption signals for physical AI: Amazon is deploying autonomous manipulation robots in warehouse workflows at large scale. This supports advisor conversations around robotics as a labor-augmentation theme, logistics automation, and the gradual movement of AI from software demos into production environments.

articles.title: Schaeffler plans to mass produce gearboxes for humanoid robots in 2027
articles.summary: Schaeffler plans to begin scaled manufacturing of formed strain wave gearboxes for humanoid robots in 2027 after completing validation testing. The company says its forming process can produce key actuator components in seconds rather than minutes, reducing manufacturing costs by more than 25% and material consumption by more than 75% versus conventional precision machining.
articles.advisor_relevance: This matters because humanoid robots depend on high-precision actuator components, and actuators can represent around half of total humanoid robot manufacturing costs. Schaeffler’s move suggests industrial suppliers are preparing for higher-volume humanoid production and that enabling components, manufacturing methods, and cost reduction may become important investment read-throughs as physical AI adoption develops.
